cohort: The study included 90 pregnant women diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus, divided into two groups.
finding: Metformin demonstrated beneficial effects on maternal and neonatal health, while the insulin treatment cohort showed a greater prevalence of inadequate glycaemic control, higher neonatal birth weight, and more infants needing phototherapy.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was significantly more common in the insulin group (75.56%) compared to the metformin group (71.11%).
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was significantly higher in the insulin group (p = 0.004), indicating a higher risk of macrosomia, but specific weight values for the cohort are not provided.
gest_age: Gestational age at delivery varied, with a higher proportion of deliveries <=37 weeks in the insulin group (15 vs 7 in metformin group), but no specific overall gestational age range for the cohort is provided.
